Pronunciation is an essential part of communication of the language. Only standard pronunciation of R.P. – Received Pronunciation helps communicate in English, though there are many dialects in English and the English spoken in different parts of the world have variations and differences.

It is imperative that students in India learn the R.P. which is the standard used by the IELTS of Cambridge while recruiting candidates for higher studies, education and immigration to the countries where English is the official language.

As the duration of this course is limited, attention is drawn towards words which are often mis-spelt, misused or mispronounced. The only sure method of learning pronunciation of English is through the recognized system of phonetic symbols. But as most of the learners in this course are not likely to have knowledge of phonetics, to use such symbols in this course would be futile and pedantic. However, for the present purpose, learning pronunciation from the instructors in the class room is the only practical option available.
English words are dependent on accents — without accents words cannot be pronounced properly. Words are formed by a single speech unit known as “Syllable”.
the word “cut” has one speech unit. Based on the syllables, words are classified into different categories.
Word with one Speech Unit (Mono syllabic words)
Ace, bay, cow, god, day, five, key, may, can, end, eight, silk, age, too, go, row, come, hear, stop etc.
Words with two Speech Units or Two Syllables (Disyllabic words)
Forward, Reward, Context, Before, Nucleus, Birthday, Pattern, Entire, Assure, Assort, Captain, Tackle, Canal, Effect, Beside, About etc.
Words with three Speech Units or three Syllables (Trisyllabic words)
Bicycle, Calculate, Educate, Accident, Quarrelsome, Recommend, Understand, Entertain, Horizon, Familiar, Deliver, Elastic etc.
Words with Four Speech Units or Four Syllables (Tetrasyllabic words)
Caterpillar, Criticism, Capitalize, Melancholy, Rhinoceros, Unfortunate, Circulation etc.
Words with Five Speech Units or Five Syllables (Pentasyllabic words)
Irregular, Co-ordinator, Communicative, Anthropology, Pronunciation, Respectively etc.
Words with more than 5 Speech Units or compound words
Indefinitely, Anticipatory, Irregularity, Tiruchirappalli, Alphabetically, Particularization etc.
There are words in which some letters are not pronounced.

‘b’ is silent as in:
comb, Womb, Limb, Bomb, Plumb, Doubt, Thumb, Debt

‘c’ is pronounced either ‘s’ or ‘k’:
as ‘s’: cell, central, century, race, vice, ace, cyanide, face, pace, rice, duce
as ‘k’: cord, come, cut, clean, music, corn, court, cover, class, connect, curfew, canal, come, capsule

‘e’ is silent as in:
alternate, gate, lapse, like, lime, prescribe, ace, age, tale, rhyme, write

‘G’ is pronounced as ‘g’ (hard) as in:
grade, grow, glide, get, girl, garage, gate, god, go, ghost, glory, goat

‘g’ is pronounced as [dʒ] (soft) as in:
germany, genuine, gypsy, gem, ginger, gentle, genetics, gypsum, gender, geography

‘gh’ is pronounced as ‘f’ in:
rough, cough, laugh, etc.

‘h’ is silent as in:
hour, honour, honest, heir, heiress, exhibit, vehicle, vehement

‘k’ is silent as in:
know, knowledge, knight, knife, knee, knack, knob, knit, knock, knuckle, etc.

‘l’ is silent as in:
alms, psalm, calm, balm, talk, walk, would, should, could, half, etc.

‘n’ is silent as in:
condemn, autumn, column

‘gh’ is silent as in:
neighbour, bright, weight, height, might, tight, right, plough

‘p’ is silent when followed by ‘s’, ‘n’ and ‘t’:
psyche, psychology, pseudonym, pneumatic, pneumonia, psalm, psalter, psychiatrist

‘t’ is silent as in:
castle, christmas, bustle, thistle, bristle, etc.

‘w’ is silent as in:
hawk, awe, row, write, wrong, wring, etc.
